title: Hotpath latency surge — hosted API P0 debrief and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2024-10-21 14:12 UTC we observed a P0-level latency spike affecting the hosted API hotpath (text generation and streaming). Symptoms included 5xx increases on the gateway (502/504), streaming stalls where clients received headers but token streams stalled for 5–20s, and elevated tail latency for non-streaming requests. The incident began ~14:12, mitigation actions began at ~14:18, traffic was routed to fallback model variants and degraded but steady service resumed by ~15:05. Full restoration (all regions and streams healthy) was confirmed by 15:30 after removing a misapplied kernel flag and cache priming.

Impact: 
- Customer-facing: ~18% of active API keys saw degraded streaming quality/interruptions for 12–45 minutes depending on region and client behavior.
- Errors: Gateway 5xx rate peaked at 11% of requests during the peak window.
- Business: Temporary SLA breaches for several customers on hosted API; several alerts escalated to customers via CS.

Detection & Pager timeline (UTC):
- 14:12 — Automated latency SLI alert (p99 > 2.5s) from hosted-api-prod-eu. Pagerduty p0 triggered.
- 14:14 — SRE on-call (Liam C) ack'd, started initial triage.
- 14:16 — Streaming error spike dashboard shows streaming consumers with stalled Read loops.
- 14:18 — Traffic shaping playbook executed: route small percentage (10%) of traffic to deduped CPU fallback tier; observed errors persist.
- 14:22 — Found simultaneous increase in host GPU kernel timeouts in serving-runtime metrics.
- 14:28 — Rolled back a recent runtime kernel flag pushed at 13:45 (quant-kernel-flag=true) across the edge pool.
- 14:35 — Partial recovery: 5xx down to 3.2%, latency improving.
- 14:50 — Began cache-priming of hot KV prefixes to accelerate subsequent requests.
- 15:05 — Majority of traffic within SLOs; streaming restored for most clients.
- 15:30 — Confirmed all regions cleared, post-incident monitoring watch started.

Root cause hypothesis: 
Primary cause: Regression in a kernel selection optimization (quant-kernel-flag=true) that was rolled out at 13:45 for a limited subset of GPUs. The optimization changed the memory access pattern for KV cache and introduced sporadic L2 cache pressure leading to elongated kernel stalls under medium-concurrency workloads.
Contributing factors: 
- Canary/control plane rollout targeted wrong fleet tags — change propagated beyond intended test GPUs.
- No automatic circuit breaker in runtime to detect elongated kernel stalls (kernel-level timeouts surfaced only at host telemetry level).
- Runbook play for streaming incidents did not include immediate kernel-flag rollback as a fast mitigation (gap in runbook).
- Cache coldness after rollback worsened token generation latency until we primed hot prefixes.

Why did it happen now?
- The flag was enabled to improve throughput on a new quantized path. Under synthetic load it looked fine but a real traffic pattern with mixture of short/long sequences and streaming read/write interleaving exposed a pathological case.

Mitigation steps taken during incident: 
1) Rapid identification of correlation between rollout time and metric deltas (Liam)
2) Scoped rollback of quant-kernel-flag across affected pool (Omar + runtime team) — immediate partial restoration
3) Traffic routing to fallback CPU/compat models for highest latency customers (Priya + Traffic Router)
4) Manual KV cache priming for hot prefixes (Hannah) — improved steady-state token latency
5) Communication: Incident channel + status page updates triggered, CS notified top 5 impacted customers by 14:40

Why mitigations worked: The rollback removed the pathological kernel behavior; fallback routing prevented mass failures while rollback propagated; cache priming addressed transient cold-cache tail latencies.

Longer-term fixes (action items):
- A1 (owner: Omar Ruiz, due 2024-11-05): Add an automatic kernel-circuit-breaker in the runtime that detects repeated kernel stalls (> X ms) and falls back to a safe kernel variant.
- A2 (owner: Priya Natarajan, due 2024-11-01): Improve rollout targeting to enforce fleet tag verification and canary windows with traffic-mirroring for 30m before full rollout.
- A3 (owner: Liam Chen, due 2024-10-31): Update streaming incident runbook to include kernel-flag rollback as a high-priority mitigation and add a triage checklist for kernel-level telemetry.
- A4 (owner: Hannah Lee, due 2024-11-07): Implement a fast KV prefix warmup utility that can be executed automatically after configuration changes or rollbacks.
- A5 (owner: SRE team, due 2024-11-15): Add a synthetic mixed-workload test harness (short+long+streaming) to nightly/regression CI for runtime kernel changes.

Runbook (draft) — high level steps for future streaming/latency spikes: 
- Triage: Confirm SLI deltas (p50/p95/p99), isolate by region and model. Check recent deployments/rollouts (control plane) for changes in last 2h.
- Kernel check: Query per-host kernel-time metrics and kernel-flag versions; if correlated, escalate to runtime oncall.
- Immediate mitigations:
  * Route 25% of traffic to fallback compat models and monitor error rate.
  * If kernel-flag suspected, perform canary rollback of that flag in smallest pool and observe.
  * If rollback improves metrics within 5–10m, continue progressive rollback.
- Streaming-specific: Restart streaming workers for affected hosts after rollback and run KV priming job.
- Communication: Open incident channel, set status page to "degraded" with affected features list, notify CS for top N customers.
- Post-incident: Start a 72h watch and collect telemetry for root-cause verification.

On-call notes and lessons learned (raw):
- Note to self: our telemetry surface needs a "kernel stall" SLO delta metric that is directly visible on the incident dashboard. Right now it's buried in host debug metrics.
- We hesitated 4–6 minutes because the optimization looked safe in synthetic tests. Next time, if change correlates with SLI regression, prefer rollback earlier.
- Rolling back flags is non-trivial if config propagation targets are wrong. We should harden tag-based gating and provide a one-click rollback that targets all currently-affected hosts.
- CS comms: customers appreciated the quick status updates but asked for adaptive ETA. Add a template for ETA estimates based on rollback vs. fallback strategies.

Open questions: 
- What threshold (X ms / repeated occurrences) constitutes a kernel stall that should trigger automatic fallback? (Action: Omar to propose thresholds by 2024-10-28)
- Can we detect cache-cold patterns earlier via sequence heatmaps? (Action: Hannah to prototype)
- Should we decouple kernel-flag rollout from service-level config rollouts to minimize blast radius?

Appendix — quick artifact links and snippets: 
- Example query used to find correlation: host_kernel_timeouts{flag="quant-kernel-flag",region="eu"} | increase() by 1m
- Temporary command to rollback flag across pool: runtime-ctl set-flag --fleet eu-hotpath --flag quant-kernel-flag=false
- Cache priming utility: tools/kv-prime --model gptx --prefixes-file /tmp/hot-prefixes.txt --parallel 20

Draft communication log (first 45m):
- 14:17 — @sre oncall posted: "Investigating elevated p99 latency in EU hosted API. Possible runtime regression. Will update in 10m"
- 14:30 — @product-notify: "Routing small % to fallback while we investigate. Next update 14:45"
- 14:40 — CS notification sent to top 5 impacted customers
- 15:10 — Status update: majority restored, continuing watch

Unresolved follow-ups for the postmortem: 
- Validate root cause via stress test (owner: runtime team) — link test plan to this doc.
- Add post-incident blameless review session with runtime + SRE (scheduled provisional: 2024-10-28).

Misc notes (informal):
- I left snippets in the incident channel that should be moved into the runtime PR for visibility.
- We should consider an emergency toggle on status page that indicates "streaming degraded" vs generic "degraded".

-- end of draft --

(Things to improve before finalizing: attach charts for p50/p95/p99, include host IDs of most-impacted machines, paste exact kernel telemetry graphs, and link to the rollback runbook snippet.)
